issues.legal_issue: Conditions imposed while granting anticipatory bail must be reasonable and relevant to securing the accused’s appearance, facilitating investigation or trial, or protecting the community, and must not be onerous, unreasonable, or excessive.

A court ordinarily cannot make payment or deposit of money allegedly involved in a private cheating dispute a condition precedent to granting anticipatory bail, because criminal proceedings cannot be used for recovery of disputed private dues.
A court may consider an accused’s voluntary offer to account for allegedly misappropriated public money before deciding a bail application where doing so serves the larger public interest.
The complainants in the alleged cheating case had no right of audience at the bail proceedings at that stage, absent a situation in which compounding the offence with the court’s permission arose.
